born.why: The code prioritizes survival by retreating when danger exceeds 90, avoids risk at moderate danger levels (75-90) unless the default is already safe, and only takes active actions when the benefit significantly outweighs the cost and danger is low (<60).

The code prioritizes survival by avoiding items that increase danger (negative cost) unless health is critical, and only heals when health drops below a safe threshold to maintain a buffer against the rising n1.

This code prioritizes survival by introducing dynamic thresholds for danger and cost, ensuring the agent retreats (a4) more aggressively as danger approaches critical levels (90) and avoiding high-cost items even when active behavior is default.

The code prioritizes survival by forcing a safe option ('a4') when danger is critical (>85), using history to identify and avoid risky item kinds, and reducing risk exposure by switching to a neutral option ('a3') when danger is moderate if the default choice is aggressive.

The rewritten code introduces dynamic risk assessment based on current danger levels (`n1`) and historical performance (`z`), allowing for more aggressive behavior in safe zones while strictly enforcing survival in critical zones, thus extending lifespan by optimizing resource acquisition without undue risk.

The code prioritizes survival by returning 'a4' at high danger and 'a3' at moderate danger, uses a stricter benefit-to-cost ratio for active options, incorporates historical failure data to avoid repeating risky actions near similar danger/cost levels, and restricts approach behavior to low-danger, low-cost scenarios.
This code tightens survival thresholds by checking pending danger (n1-n2) and reducing action frequency as n1 rises, prioritizing low-cost items to prevent n1 from increasing rapidly.

The original code unnecessarily rejected beneficial items when `n2` was high, which is suboptimal because reducing `n1` (damage) is always good for longevity as long as `n2` remains positive. The rewrite simplifies logic to strictly accept any item that reduces `n1` and rejects harmful or neutral items, maximizing survival by consistently lowering damage whenever possible.
